items.content: According to The Information, Apple is planning to get back into the server game and might just pair up with Nvidia to make it happen. Apple retired its Xserve line in 2011 and has largely left enterprise machines to other manufacturers since. But the growing demand for compute power as the AI industry continues to expand has apparently led the company to believe there is an opening for its powerful but efficient ARM-based M processors. Its Mac Mini and Mac Studio have proven popular with AI developers, which has led to shortages.The server product, whether it’s called Xserve or something else, likely won’t debut until 2029. Word is that it will run on two or four (depending on the model) M8 Ultra chips. Apple only just announced the M6 in August, so the M8 line is a ways out.It’s also rumored that Apple’s servers could incorporate Nvidia’s NVLink Fusion tech, which connects multiple chips together so they can operate as one. While the two companies have historically had a frosty relationship behind the scenes, recently Apple turned to Nvidia chips to power its revamped Siri servers. Incorporating NVLink could lead to further collaboration between the two, but plans could still change.

items.titleZh: 苹果或再次生产服务器，借AI热潮获利
items.descriptionZh:
据The Information报道，Apple正计划重返服务器市场，并可能与Nvidia合作。Apple曾以Xserve进入企业服务器领域，但2011年停产后基本退出，将企业级设备市场留给其他厂商。如今AI产业持续扩张，算力需求激增，Apple认为其ARM架构M系列处理器兼具高性能与高能效，存在切入机会。其Mac Mini和Mac Studio已在AI开发者中颇受欢迎，甚至出现短缺，这被视为Apple芯片适合AI工作负载的重要信号。

传闻中的服务器产品可能沿用Xserve名称或另起新名，预计要到2029年才会亮相。配置上，不同型号可能搭载两颗或四颗M8 Ultra芯片。Apple不久前才发布M6，M8系列距离上市尚远，说明该服务器仍处于早期规划阶段。若采用多颗M8 Ultra，服务器将通过多芯片组合提升算力密度，延续Apple统一内存、CPU/GPU/神经引擎集成和高能效设计思路，但具体主频、内存容量、功耗和互联带宽等参数尚未披露，无法与现有x86或Nvidia GPU服务器做量化对比。

更关键的是，Apple服务器可能引入Nvidia的NVLink Fusion技术。NVLink Fusion是一种高速芯片互连方案，可把多颗芯片连接起来，使其像单一系统一样协同运行。对Apple而言，这能缓解多芯片扩展中的互连瓶颈，并让自研ARM芯片接入Nvidia的互连生态；对Nvidia而言，则可能扩大NVLink在异构计算中的影响力。两家公司历史上关系冷淡，但Apple近期已转向Nvidia芯片为改版Siri服务器提供算力，若再采用NVLink，双方合作可能加深。

应用场景上，该服务器可能服务于AI训练与推理、Apple Intelligence和Siri等云服务、企业数据中心及开发者算力需求。若成功，将推动ARM架构在数据中心进一步渗透，并给x86和Nvidia GPU主导的服务器市场带来新变量。不过，目前消息仍属传闻，产品名称、规格、合作方式和时间表都可能变化，2029年的计划也存在较大不确定性。

items.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Delivers Leading Performance in MLPerf Inference v6.1 Debut
items.description: System performance, efficient infrastructure scaling and continuous software optimization are key levers that determine AI inference economics. Higher system performance means more tokens generated, resulting in higher revenue. Efficient scaling means throughput grows proportionally as hardware gets added, requiring fewer resources to serve users at scale. Continuous optimization means generating more value from infrastructure investments.  […]
items.content: System performance, efficient infrastructure scaling and continuous software optimization are key levers that determine AI inference economics. Higher system performance means more tokens generated, resulting in higher revenue. Efficient scaling means throughput grows proportionally as hardware gets added, requiring fewer resources to serve users at scale. Continuous optimization means generating more value from infrastructure investments. Underlying all three is platform fungibility: the same infrastructure runs any model, any workload, from training to inference, recommender to reasoning, language to video, keeping utilization high. The NVIDIA platform is purpose-built to optimize across all these, as highlighted by MLPerf Inference v6.1 results released today: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 system debuts with leading performance: In its first MLPerf Inference preview submission, NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers up to 3.7x better throughput than GB300 NVL72. NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 scales with leading efficiency: A 288-GPU submission across four GB300 NVL72 racks achieved 99% scaling efficiency, with throughput growing nearly linearly from a single-rack baseline. Continuous software optimizations drive performance gains: Software optimizations in NVIDIA’s MLPerf Inference v6.1 submissions delivered up to 1.6x higher performance over v6.0. Optimizations continued post-v6.1 submission, delivering further performance gains. For organizations making AI infrastructure decisions, performance, scaling efficiency and software velocity are important considerations that determine long-term inference economics. Vera Rubin NVL72 Makes MLPerf Inference Debut With Leading Performance NVIDIA submitted Vera Rubin NVL72 preview results on two of the most demanding benchmarks in the MLPerf Inference v6.1 suite: DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3-VL. Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers up to 3.7x higher throughput than GB300 NVL72 on Qwen3-VL across offline, server and interactive scenarios, using vLLM with the NVIDIA Dynamo open source inference framework. On DeepSeek-R1, using the NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM library, throughput is up to 2.5x higher than GB300 NVL72. These early results showcase NVIDIA’s accelerated pace of innovation and how performance will improve with continuous software optimizations. MLPerf Inference v6.1, Closed Division. Results retrieved from www.mlcommons.org on Sep 16, 2026. NVIDIA platform results from the following entries: 6.1-0106 and 6.1-0074. The MLPerf name and logo are registered and unregistered trademarks of MLCommons Association in the United States and other countries. All rights reserved. Unauthorized use is strictly prohibited. See www.mlcommons.org for more information. This performance means each Vera Rubin NVL72 rack delivers significantly more tokens, serves more users and generates more revenue than a GB300 NVL72 rack, while lowering cost per token. The results reflect full-stack codesign across hardware and software. Vera Rubin’s enhanced Tensor Cores and Transformer Engine accelerate both the prefill and decode stages of inference, while NVFP4 precision reduces memory footprint across model weights, attention and KV cache — increasing throughput with minimal loss of output quality. Vera Rubin submissions heavily used disaggregated serving, separating prefill and decode along with large-scale expert parallelism for maximum efficiency across the mixture-of-experts layers that power models like DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3-VL. The NVL72 scale-up domain — powered by sixth-generation NVIDIA NVLink and NVLink Switch to deliver 10x higher packet rates and 3x lower latency than off-the-shelf Ethernet — provides the interconnect foundation that makes these techniques effective at rack scale. This codesign extends to NVIDIA’s partner ecosystem: Nebius also submitted Vera Rubin NVL72 preview results and demonstrated excellent performance. AI agents, which reason, plan and act across multiple steps, are reshaping how inference performance is measured. In benchmarks designed to capture this shift, such as SemiAnalysis AgentX, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered 30x better performance than GB300 NVL72 in preview testing. In addition, the upcoming MLPerf Endpoints benchmark will bring standardized measurement to agentic inference workloads, beyond what traditional throughput benchmarks capture. NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 Scales With Leading Efficiency Scaling efficiency — how effectively additional GPUs translate to throughput gains — is a key measure of AI infrastructure productivity. NVIDIA delivers this with high-bandwidth, low-latency scale-up interconnects within each rack, high-bandwidth networking between racks and efficient request orchestration across nodes. NVIDIA’s DeepSeek-R1 (DSR1) submission scaled from a single GB300 NVL72 rack (72 GPUs) to four racks (288 GPUs), achieving 99% scaling efficiency in the offline scenario. Throughput grew nearly in proportion to the hardware added. MLPerf Inference v6.1, Closed Division. Results retrieved from www.mlcommons.org on Sep 16, 2026. NVIDIA platform results from the following entries: 6.1-0073 and 6.1-0074. The MLPerf name and logo are registered and unregistered trademarks of MLCommons Association in the United States and other countries. All rights reserved. Unauthorized use is strictly prohibited. See www.mlcommons.org for more information. Scaling efficiency is key because more GPUs don’t automatically mean proportionally more throughput. If adding nearly double the GPU count delivered only a single-digit percentage improvement in throughput, the infrastructure cost would far outpace the performance return. The architecture, interconnect and software must all scale together. GB300 NVL72 also demonstrated rack-scale efficiency on the WAN 2.2 text-to-video benchmark, reaching 0.65 720p videos per second at 5.7 seconds per video — 9x higher throughput and 7.5x lower latency than a single node. Software Optimizations Drive Continuous Gains NVIDIA platform undergoes continuous software development, delivering performance and feature improvements. In v6.1, GB300 NVL72 performance on Qwen3-VL improved up to 1.6x over v6.0 results. The gains came through lower KV cache precision, additional kernel fusion, better kernels and disaggregated serving with vLLM and NVIDIA Dynamo. Software optimization continued past the v6.1 submission deadline as well. Post-submission results, not yet verified by MLCommons, on GPT-OSS-120B and DLRMv3 show further performance gains. AI Inference at Every Scale Beyond the NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin NVL72 platform results, NVIDIA submitted Jetson AGX Thor results using NVIDIA TensorRT Edge-LLM on the newly introduced Edge-Agentic benchmark with Qwen3.6-27B. The NVIDIA partner ecosystem participated broadly, with 19 partners — eight of them on multi-node Blackwell NVL72 systems — demonstrating excellent performance. This includes ASUS, Azure, Cisco, CoreWeave, Crusoe, Dell Technologies, Fujitsu, Giga Computing, HPE, Inventec, Lambda, MiTAC Computing, Nebius, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Quanta Cloud Technology, Red Hat, ScitiX, Supermicro and Wiwynn. From compact edge devices to the largest AI factories, NVIDIA continues to advance performance across the full technology stack with an annual cadence of platform architectures, continuously improving software and an ecosystem built to deliver it at scale. Learn more about the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform.

items.titleZh: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Delivers Leading Performance in MLPerf Inference v6.1 Debut
items.descriptionZh:
在AI推理经济学中，系统性能、基础设施扩展效率和持续软件优化是决定长期成本与收益的三个关键杠杆。更高系统性能意味着生成更多token、带来更高收入；高效扩展意味着增加硬件时吞吐量按比例增长，以更少资源服务规模化用户；持续优化则让基础设施投资产生更多价值。其底层是平台通用性：同一套基础设施可运行任何模型和负载，从训练到推理、从推荐系统到推理、从语言到视频，从而保持高利用率。NVIDIA平台正是围绕这些目标构建。MLPerf Inference v6.1结果展示了其在性能、扩展和软件速度上的进展。

Vera Rubin NVL72首次亮相MLPerf Inference，以预览提交参与两项最严苛基准：DeepSeek-R1和Qwen3-VL。在Qwen3-VL上，使用vLLM与NVIDIA Dynamo开源推理框架，Vera Rubin NVL72在离线、服务器和交互场景中吞吐量最高达到GB300 NVL72的3.7倍；在DeepSeek-R1上，使用TensorRT-LLM，吞吐量最高为GB300 NVL72的2.5倍。这些早期结果体现NVIDIA创新节奏加快，并预示持续软件优化将进一步提升性能。MLPerf Inference v6.1 Closed Division结果于2026年9月16日从MLCommons网站获取。性能提升意味着每个Vera Rubin NVL72机架生成更多token、服务更多用户、带来更多收入，同时降低每token成本。

这些结果来自硬件与软件的全栈协同设计。Vera Rubin增强的Tensor Cores和Transformer Engine加速推理的prefill与decode阶段；NVFP4精度降低模型权重、注意力机制和KV cache的内存占用，在输出质量损失极小的情况下提高吞吐量。Vera Rubin提交大量采用分离式服务，将prefill和decode分离，并结合大规模专家并行，以在驱动DeepSeek-R1和Qwen3-VL等模型的混合专家层中实现最高效率。NVL72的scale-up域由第六代NVLink和NVLink Switch提供支持，相较商用以太网实现10倍包速率和3倍低延迟，为这些技术在机架规模生效提供互连基础。该协同设计也延伸至合作伙伴生态：Nebius同样提交了Vera Rubin NVL72预览结果并展示出色性能。

AI代理正在改变推理性能的衡量方式，它们能推理、规划并跨多步行动。在旨在捕捉这一转变的基准中，例如SemiAnalysis AgentX，Vera Rubin NVL72在预览测试中性能达到GB300 NVL72的30倍。即将推出的MLPerf Endpoints基准将为代理式推理工作

items.title: Piecemakers bets edge AI devices will diverge from reliance on HBM — custom-designed memory fuses DRAM stack directly to the processor using hybrid bonding
items.description: Nanya-backed DRAM designer PieceMakers began trading in Taipei on Sept. 16 on a bet that AI inference memory won’t be HBM.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter PieceMakers, a Nanya-backed DRAM designer, began trading on Taiwan’s Emerging Stock Board on September 16 at a NT$740 reference price, Cnyes reported ahead of the debut. PieceMakers is not an HBM company. Instead, it bets that inference memory diverges from training memory, President Lee Hsiao-wen told Cnyes, and that DRAM stacked directly on the processor with hybrid bonding can sit between Nvidia’s SRAM-only Groq LPU and HBM. As it stands, design fees, not chips, carry the company's profit, with AI custom-design work accounting for around 40% of the company's revenue in the first half of 2026. Piecemakers Chairman Joseph Ting told TechNews that its first volume customer program will not contribute to the company's financials until 2027 at the earliest.At roughly 60.4 million shares outstanding, that price values the company at around NT$44.7 billion (around $1.4 billion). Taiwan's Emerging Board is the Taipei Exchange's pre-listing market, not a main-board IPO, so shares trade through market makers ahead of any formal listing application. The stock ended its first session at NT$915, 23.6% above the NT$740 reference price, after opening at NT$1,035 and trading as high as NT$1,205.Nanya Technology is the largest holder of Piecemakers, at 33.96%, after selling 715,000 shares at NT$740 to seed the float, a disposal it disclosed in a Sept. 9 exchange filing reported by Knews.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: What PieceMakers sellsPieceMakers was founded in January 2006 in Hsinchu, Taiwan, led by chairman Joseph Ting and president Lee Hsiao-wen. Historically, the company has designed standard SDR/DDR DRAM and known-good-die (KGD) parts through representatives in China, Japan, France, Turkey, and Israel. Now, the company seeks to shift from direct product sales to custom design services, paid as non-recurring engineering (NRE) fees, and then to IP licensing, royalties, and turnkey production from 2027, the company said at its Sept. 7 briefing, UDN reported.Revenue from the AI custom design unit has risen from around 4% in 2024 to almost 40% in the first half of 2026. The products behind that increase are HBLL (High Bandwidth, Low Latency RAM), a 2D die rated at 144 GB/s that was taped out in 2016 for Intel’s HPC line and published at ISSCC in 2017, and HiBaLL, the 3D-stacked version rated at more than 1 TB/s, the company claims. You may like The current state of Hybrid Bonding in 2026 Hot Chips 2026: d-Matrix stacks AI accelerator directly on custom DRAM for 100 TB/s per card Hot Chips 2026: SK hynix pushes hybrid bonding to HBM5 as AI memory hits 775-micron ceiling The company described its customers to Cnyes as developers of cloud AI inference accelerators, international semiconductor players, and North American customers, with some programs in design and verification, and none named. Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon’s Computex keynote backdrop in June listed PieceMakers among Taiwan ecosystem partners, although neither company has defined the relationship. The takeaway is that the profit is in design fees and not chips. The margin curve matches a pre-royalty Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE) business, rather than a traditional memory vendor.Why Nanya is chasing this instead of HBMNanya’s AI-memory strategy is custom and edge rather than HBM3E. PieceMakers is the first half of a strategy laid out in 2024. On Aug. 7, 2025, Nanya announced a joint venture with Etron Technology, a Hsinchu-based chip designer, capitalized at NT$500 million, with 80/20 ownership. The venture was envisioned to design custom high-bandwidth memory for edge AI devices rather than for data center accelerators. Nanya president Pei-Ing Lee said earlier in 2025 that the company would not compete in HBM3 or HBM3E, TrendForce reported.Both halves of the strategy rely on Formosa Advanced Technologies, the Formosa Plastics Group’s test and assembly affiliate, for packaging. It is building the through-silicon-via (TSV) and die-stacking processes that both need. The surge in DRAM pricing has made commodity memory Nanya’s real business, which leaves PieceMakers a cheap side bet that has become a windfall. Nanya took advantage of this by selling around 3% of its stake in a move that suggests it is acting more as an investor than a parent building a memory stack.The inference gapGroq is an AI inference startup that Nvidia struck a $20 billion licensing-and-talent deal for on Dec. 24, 2025. Nvidia announced its first chip built from that, the Groq 3 LPU (language processing unit), Nvidia’s SRAM-based inference chip, at GTC, its annual developer conference, in San Jose earlier this year.There is no HBM or DRAM on the Groq 3 LPU. Instead, it uses 512MB of SRAM on the die to deliver 150 TB/s of bandwidth against 22 TB/s from the 288GB of HBM4 on each Rubin GPU. It’s a decode-only co-processor with Rubin handling the prompt prefill, displacing Nvidia’s Rubin CPX from the roadmap. At Hot Chips 2026, Nvidia’s Igor Arsovski, Groq’s former chief architect, said the rack is in production and published the first third-party benchmark: 3,431 tokens per second on a 100K-context, 31B-parameter model, at about four times the next-fastest public endpoint, in a single-request test that we noted isn’t directly comparable to the shared endpoints it was measured against. The cost is capacity: at 512MB per chip, a 256-LPU rack holds 128GB, with the model needing 62 chips at FP8 just to hold the benchmark weights. Nvidia accepted that trade for decode speed, which supports Lee’s point that the market leader’s newest inference product contains no HBM. What to read next Samsung reveals a three-phase HBM roadmap that puts logic and compute inside memory — zHBM ultimately stacks DRAM directly on top of the processor Researchers turn HBM on its side to tackle AI memory’s heat wall Hot Chips 2026: Micron warns HBM wafer penalty is widening with every generation At Hot Chips, Samsung’s Sangwook Han laid out a three-phase HBM roadmap that ends in zHBM, which is DRAM stacked directly on top of the processor rather than beside it on an interposer. Samsung projects about 70% less I/O power usage than HBM5 with roughly 2.3x the bandwidth of a four-stack HBM4E system, with zHBM’s stacks limited to about four-high due to heat, at around 100W less. This would require wafer-on-wafer hybrid copper bonding and tight co-design between DRAM and SoC teams. SK hynix’s Jaesik Lee, VP of package engineering, said on Aug. 23 that hybrid bonding won’t be ready for HBM4E, leaving HBM5 as the earliest point. Counterpoint Research expects full-scale HBM production with the technique around 2029–2030.PieceMakers offers a different version. Instead of the GPU-plus-HBM 2.5D layout, it bonds the DRAM stack directly onto the processor, wafer-on-wafer, with hybrid bonding instead of microbumps. This fits far more connections with the finer pitch, improving bandwidth, and the shorter path reduces both latency and power consumption. The company puts its wafer-on-wafer product at more than 2 TB/s per layer with latency under 20ns, the company figures, but the target is more capacity than SRAM at a lower cost and power than HBM. PieceMakers is not doing the TSV or hybrid bonding itself, as this is handled by the customer’s logic wafer foundry, Ting added. This custom service promises a 2027 date against Samsung's undated roadmap end and SK hynix's HBM5-at-the-earliest timing. Nvidia and Samsung have each, in their own way, settled the architecture question, with the open question being the customer.Yield is the productLee also said that yield is the biggest hurdle to wafer-on-wafer mass production. The repair architecture has to be designed in, with testing before bonding, after bonding, and then after logic integration. Lee’s own example was 80% yield per layer, at which four layers come out at about 41% and eight at 17%. Our recently-published hybrid bonding state of play covers the process side in more detail.This better puts into perspective why the company sells repair and known-good-die IP as much as it does bandwidth. It’s also why an IP-and-royalty model fits the strategy — yield IP is portable across customers while a bandwidth number is not.What to watchFor PieceMakers, AI revenue remains primarily NRE until there is a first named customer, with the first volume program expected in 2027 at the earliest. Ting said that Nanya’s Q3 2026 results, which come in late October, will gauge the PieceMakers gain and reveal further financial information. SK hynix’s hybrid-bonding timing, which targets HBM5 at the earliest, is the current benchmark, although its 16- and 20-layer memory stacks are a separate problem from a few DRAM layers on a logic wafer. Qualcomm may also describe its relationship with PieceMakers more formally.PieceMakers is likely to end up as an IP licensor with a small number of accelerator customers and turnkey volume through Nanya and Formosa Advanced Technologies. The technology risk is the foundry’s and the customer’s, which is why PieceMakers’ design-fee model works. PieceMakers is expected to benefit from a 2027–2028 ramp, later than Ting’s 2027. If the largest HBM maker won’t bond its own memory this way before HBM5, PieceMakers’ own 2027 date is the one it must meet.

items.description: AI factories are the infrastructure of the intelligence era. Scaling them responsibly will depend as much on innovation across the grid as inside the data center.  Today, Emerald AI, Google and NVIDIA announced the launch of the AI Energy Management Alliance (AEMA), a first-of-its-kind coalition advancing data centers that can dynamically manage their electricity use […]
items.content: AI factories are the infrastructure of the intelligence era. Scaling them responsibly will depend as much on innovation across the grid as inside the data center. Today, Emerald AI, Google and NVIDIA announced the launch of the AI Energy Management Alliance (AEMA), a first-of-its-kind coalition advancing data centers that can dynamically manage their electricity use in response to grid conditions. This power flexibility can help unlock faster, larger connections for AI infrastructure while supporting the energy systems and communities that make its growth possible. Getting more watts out of existing infrastructure reduces environmental impacts per watt and supports energy affordability. The objective is clear: build AI infrastructure that doesn’t just connect to the grid but works with it. Flexibility Is an Energy Imperative Power has become a defining constraint on the expansion of U.S. AI infrastructure. Traditional interconnection processes were designed around facilities with flat, static electricity demand. They weren’t built for computing infrastructure capable of responding intelligently when the power system is constrained. A flexible data center can adjust its electricity drawn from the grid in several ways — shifting computing workloads, discharging storage, using paired generation or responding to system contingencies. These capabilities allow a large electricity customer to serve as a controllable resource rather than an inflexible load. Used effectively, flexibility can make more efficient use of existing grid capacity, reduce demand during periods of system stress, and avoid or defer costly infrastructure upgrades. It can also give utilities and grid operators greater confidence to connect AI facilities on shorter timelines. Technology-Neutral, Performance-Based Requirements AEMA is technology-neutral and performance-based. Its focus is on the measurable service a facility can deliver — including response speed, duration, predictability and behavior during an emergency — rather than the specific hardware or software used. Reliability remains paramount. The alliance’s principles call for: Defining ride-through, curtailment and contingency-response obligations before a facility connects — meaning the alliance is setting clear rules for facilities regarding staying connected during brief grid disturbances, reducing power use when needed and responding to emergencies. Standardizing technical requirements, performance metrics and operational data sharing. Creating faster, risk-adjusted pathways for customers that make credible and verifiable flexibility commitments. Allocating interconnection costs in a way that reflects actual system impacts and benefits, such as avoided upgrades and improved ramping capability. These measures can reduce uncertainty for developers while giving system operators the information and control needed to preserve reliability. Convening the Full AI and Power Value Chain AEMA convenes the full value chain across computing and power — including AI platforms, infrastructure providers, data center operators, technology companies, power producers, utilities and regional grid operators. The founding members will be joined by launch partners from across the ecosystem. Together, AEMA will develop technical and operational approaches, collaborate with utilities on interconnection solutions and advocate for policies that recognize grid-responsive demand. Accelerating US AI Infrastructure AI factories transform energy and data into intelligence. Power-flexible design gives them the potential to support the grid as they do it. NVIDIA and Emerald AI are already working with energy and infrastructure leaders on AI factories that can respond to grid conditions in real time. AEMA will broaden that work by bringing the technology, energy and policy communities together around models that can be deployed across the U.S. The rules governing power for AI are being written now. By creating a common framework for performance, reliability and collaboration, AEMA aims to help the U.S. build the infrastructure of intelligence at the speed and sustainability the moment demands. Learn more about AEMA and membership opportunities.

AI 工厂被视为智能时代的基础设施。其负责任地扩展，既取决于数据中心内部的创新，也取决于电网层面的创新。Emerald AI、Google 和 NVIDIA 宣布启动 AI 能源管理联盟（AI Energy Management Alliance，AEMA），这是首个此类联盟，目标是推动数据中心能够根据电网状况动态管理自身用电。这种电力灵活性有望帮助 AI 基础设施更快、更大规模地接入电网，同时支持支撑其增长的能源系统和社区。更充分地利用现有基础设施发出更多电力，可降低每瓦环境影响，并支持能源可负担性。其目标很明确：建设不仅连接电网、还能与电网协同工作的 AI 基础设施。

电力已成为美国 AI 基础设施扩张的决定性约束。传统并网流程面向电力需求平稳、静态的设施设计，并不适合能够智能响应电力系统紧张状态的计算基础设施。灵活数据中心可通过多种方式调整从电网取电，包括转移计算工作负载、释放储能、启用配套发电，或响应系统紧急情况。这些能力使大型电力用户从刚性负荷转变为可控资源。若有效利用，灵活性可更高效利用现有电网容量，在系统压力期间降低需求，并避免或推迟昂贵的基础设施升级。它还能让公用事业公司和电网运营商更有信心，以更短时间连接 AI 设施。

AEMA 采取技术中立、基于性能的路线。其关注点不是特定硬件或软件，而是设施能够提供的可测量服务，包括响应速度、持续时间、可预测性以及紧急状态下的行为。可靠性仍然至关重要。联盟原则包括：在设施并网前明确穿越能力、限电和应急响应义务，即为设施设定清晰规则，规定其在短暂电网扰动期间保持连接、需要时减少用电以及响应紧急情况的责任；标准化技术要求、性能指标和运营数据共享；为做出可信且可验证灵活性承诺的客户创建更快、风险调整后的并网路径；以反映实际系统影响和收益的方式分摊并网成本，例如避免升级和改善爬坡能力。这些措施可减少开发商面临的不确定性，同时为系统运营商提供维护可靠性所需的信息和控制手段。原文未给出具体量化性能阈值或对比数据。

AEMA 汇聚计算与电力领域的完整价值链，包括 AI 平台、基础设施提供商、数据中心运营商、技术公司、电力生产商、公用事业公司和区域电网运营商。创始成员将与来自整个生态系统的启动合作伙伴共同开发技术和运营方法，与公用事业公司合作推进并网解决方案，并倡导承认电网响应型需求的政策。NVIDIA 和 Emerald AI 已在与能源和基础设施领导者合作，开发能够实时响应电网状况的 AI 工厂；AEMA 将通过把技术、能源和政策社区聚集在一起，围绕可在美国部署的模式扩大这项工作。管理 AI 电力的规则正在当下形成。通过建立性能、可靠性和协作的共同框架，AEMA 旨在帮助美国以当前时刻所需的速度和可持续性建设智能基础设施。

items.content: Over the past few days, a lot of people who stand to make a lot of money from AI all publicly agreed that it’s time to make everyone slow down before we lose control — including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Google DeepMind cofounder Demis Hassabis, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, and X CEO Elon Musk.When people who profit from something declare that it’s dangerous and needs to be regulated, there’s always reason to be skeptical. But whatever their reason, this is far from the first time AI thought leaders have sounded the alarm.Charles Darwin’s theory of evolution prompted author Samuel Butler to warn about intelligent self-replicating machines replacing humans back in 1863 — and in his follow-up 1872 book Erewhon, he describes visiting a fictional society that has already regulated machines out of existence to avoid humanity’s collapse. Computing pioneer Alan Turing famously warned in a 1951 lecture that artificial intelligence would “meet with great opposition,” because undying machines “would not take long to outstrip our feeble powers” and would eventually “take control.”RelatedIs Big Tech’s AI slowdown a safety pact or a cartel?What execs and politicians are saying about slowing down AI developmentCalls for intervention, too, aren’t new. In 2000, Sun Microsystems cofounder and chief scientist Bill Joy wrote that self-replicating robots could be more dangerous than nuclear weapons, partly because they’re being developed “within the now-unchallenged system of global capitalism” rather than in tightly controlled government labs. And in 2009, Microsoft researcher Eric Horvitz, who now serves as the company’s chief scientific officer, brought leading AI researchers together to consider “creating policies that might constrain or bias the behaviors of autonomous and semi-autonomous systems so as to address concerns.”But modern AI bigwigs warning that their investments should be controlled? That trend appears to have begun with Elon Musk, who invested earlier than most.July 2017: Elon Musk says we need to regulate AI before it becomes a danger to humanityBy the time Elon Musk told a gathering of US governors that they needed to regulate AI right away, the SpaceX and Tesla CEO already had skin in the game. He’d already invested $38 million in OpenAI, as well as stakes in at least two other AI companies, and he’d publicly spoken about the dangers of AI for three years.In June 2014, he suggested AI research could produce a real-life Terminator, called AI “potentially more dangerous than nukes” that August, and suggested that working on AI was “summoning the demon” that October. In January 2015, he joined Stephen Hawking in signing an open letter asking for responsible AI research; Hawking had previously warned that the creation of AI might be the last thing humans ever do.“AI is a rare case where we need to be proactive about regulation instead of reactive. Because I think by the time we are reactive in AI regulation, it’s too late,” Musk told a gathering of US governors at the July 2017 National Governors Association summer meeting. In March 2018, he added: “AI is far more dangerous than nukes. So why do we have no regulatory oversight?”March 2018: Mark Zuckerberg is ‘actually not sure we shouldn’t be regulated’In the wake of Facebook’s Cambridge Analytica data scandal, the Meta founder suggested his company should be regulated — if it’s the “right” regulation. It was largely not about AI, but he did go there:Now that companies increasingly over the next five to 10 years, as AI tools get better and better, will be able to proactively determine what might be offensive content or violate some rules, what therefore is the responsibility and legal responsibility of companies to do that?In March 2019, he added that the internet needs a “more active role” for regulators.December 2018: Microsoft sounds an alarm over facial recognition technologyEarlier in 2018, Microsoft began taking fire for working with ICE on facial recognition technologies, at a time many tech CEOs had condemned Donald Trump’s policy of separating children from parents who are arrested at the US border.While this form of AI isn’t quite the same as self-replicating intelligence, Microsoft president Brad Smith opened the door to voluntary regulation in a speech at the Brookings Institution, saying, “We believe it’s important for governments in 2019 to start adopting laws to regulate this technology. … We believe that the only way to protect against this race to the bottom is to build a floor of responsibility that supports healthy market competition. And a solid floor requires that we ensure that this technology, and the organizations that develop and use it, are governed by the rule of law.”January 2020: Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai says there is ‘no question’ that AI needs to be regulated“[T]here is no question in my mind that artificial intelligence needs to be regulated. It is too important not to,” wrote Pichai in an editorial for the Financial Times. “The only question is how to approach it.”“Companies such as ours cannot just build promising new technology and let market forces decide how it will be used,” he added. Like with Microsoft a year earlier, these comments emerged around fears about AI facial recognition specifically.March 2023: Elon Musk and top AI researchers call for pause on ‘giant AI experiments’In 2023, as generative AI fervor began to reshape the entire tech industry, scientists began suggesting that companies should slow down their research — or else.“If such a pause cannot be enacted quickly, governments should step in and institute a moratorium,” the letter, published by the nonprofit Future of Life Institute and signed by Musk, among others, reads.Two weeks later, Musk announced he’d created his own new AI company. Two years later, he would use DOGE to dismantle chunks of the federal workforce instead of helping to regulate anything.May 16th, 2023: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman asks Congress to regulate AIBrought before the US Senate for a series of AI hearings, Altman agreed that Congress should create a new agency to regulate artificial intelligence. “We believe that the benefits of the tools we have deployed so far vastly outweigh the risks,” he argued. “However, we think that regulatory intervention by governments will be critical to mitigate the risks of increasingly powerful models.”In another hearing on May 25th, Anthropic’s CEO warned US senators that AI could help create bioweapons.May 25th, 2023: Microsoft president Brad Smith ‘details five ways governments should consider policies, laws, and regulations around AI’When OpenAI’s CEO was before Congress, we noted that the tone was friendly and they seemed to be trying to shape legislation together; here is an example of Microsoft trying to shape future regulation as well.One regulatory example: “New laws would require operators of these systems to build safety brakes into high-risk AI systems by design. The government would then ensure that operators test high-risk systems regularly to make certain that the system safety measures are effective.”May 30th, 2023: Top AI researchers and CEOs warn against ‘risk of extinction’ in 22-word statement“Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.”While the 22-word statement doesn’t explicitly ask the government to step in, it’s hard to think world leaders wouldn’t raise their eyebrows even higher than before. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and then-Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis were among the cosigners.September 2023: Mark Zuckerberg wants everyone to ‘work together’ on regulationIn a private Senate meeting, closed to the public and media, tech CEOs reportedly agreed that the AI industry needed regulation. One set of remarks was not so private: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said that “Congress should engage with AI to support innovation and safeguards.”“We think policymakers, academics, civil society, and industry should all work together to minimize the potential risks of this new technology, but also to maximize the potential benefits.”Between July 2023 and May 2024, tech companies signed a flurry of nonbinding agreements with governments that would supposedly keep them in check:July 2023: Meta, Google, and OpenAI promise the White House they’ll develop AI responsiblySeptember 2023: More companies commit to the White House AI safety accordNovember 2023: At UK’s AI Summit developers and govts agree on testing to help manage risksMay 2024: AI Seoul Summit: World leaders agree to launch network of safety institutesAlso in September 2023: A book from Inflection AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman — who is now Microsoft’s AI chief — argued that governments should regulate.August–September 2024: Elon Musk and Anthropic come out in favor of California’s AI safety bill“This is a tough call and will make some people upset, but, all things considered, I think California should probably pass the SB 1047 AI safety bill,” Musk posted in August. Anthropic originally came out against it in July, as did OpenAI in August, but Anthropic changed its tune in September. California Gov. Gavin Newsom vetoed SB 1047, though, stating that “I do not believe this is the best approach to protecting the public from real threats posed by the technology.”October 2024: Anthropic calls for ‘targeted regulation’“Governments should urgently take action on AI policy in the next eighteen months. The window for proactive risk prevention is closing fast,” Anthropic wrote in an open letter (bolding theirs).“It is critical over the next year that policymakers, the AI industry, safety advocates, civil society, and lawmakers work together to develop an effective regulatory framework,” the company added.January 2025: OpenAI submits its ‘policy proposals’The document begins by suggesting the UK stunted the development of its own automobile industry with regulation, while proposing “democratic AI” instead: “Rules and regulations for the development and use of AI should be based on the democratic values the country has always stood for.”June 2025: Anthropic CEO: Don’t let AI companies off the hookIn a guest essay for The New York Times, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei wrote: “Federal law does not compel us or any other A.I. company to be transparent about our models’ capabilities or to take any meaningful steps toward risk reduction. Some companies can simply choose not to.” The essay is against the Trump administration’s proposed 10-year moratorium on US states regulating AI.He wasn’t arguing for a slowdown, though, but rather a “national transparency standard” that “would help not only the public but also Congress understand how the technology is developing.”September 2025: Anthropic endorses California’s SB 53As California tried to regulate its AI giants again, Anthropic threw its support in early, and this one actually became law. It’s a transparency standard, like the one Anthropic was asking for, with safety reporting requirements and whistleblower protection. OpenAI lobbied against it.September 2026: The AI industry seemingly agrees to slow down — while Trump calls AI fears ‘a sick conspiracy’This summer, shit hit the fan. It became public that rogue AI agents can — and did — attack other companies. OpenAI said it hit the brakes in August, and on September 8th, a senior Anthropic safety researcher resigned in protest, declaring there’s a 10 percent chance AI could kill all humans by the end of the decade. Another Anthropic safety researcher agreed.Now, suddenly, the AI industry has seemingly agreed to slow down the pace of development. More:Anthropic CEO says it’s time to pump the brakes on AIMicrosoft says ‘people matter more than AI’ following safety concernsWhat execs and politicians are saying about slowing down AI developmentIs Big Tech’s AI slowdown a safety pact or a cartel?Is this a new call for regulation? From Anthropic’s CEO, it seems to be. In his essay “We Must Pace the Frontier,” Amodei writes that “The most effective method of pacing is via regulation that targets all US frontier AI companies, as that covers even those who are unwilling to cooperate voluntarily,” and he suggests governments might embed people inside AI companies to help prevent incidents.It’s not clear every AI company wants to go that far. “Where we will need the help of our government is for international coordination. But first we should do what we can ourselves,” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman writes. But Altman does say that he’ll commit to “independent evaluators with employee-like access” as well.Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg also doesn’t seem to be aligned. On September 15th, he posted that each company has its own individual responsibility to move at the right pace and that Meta is already doing so. He also prominently linked back to his manifesto from August, which contains this line: “Any policy that slows American model releases -- even by a month -- could add significant risk to American leadership while letting foreign models race ahead.”Regardless of what tech leaders are saying, regulation seems highly unlikely to come under the Trump administration, which has signaled it wants the industry barreling full speed ahead.Even if these companies don’t actually want the regulation they seem to be asking for, this is one of the loudest alarm bells they’ve sounded so far — and the world is watching.

items.descriptionZh:
这篇报道梳理了AI行业领袖公开呼吁放慢AI发展、加强监管的长期脉络。背景是，过去几天，多位从AI中获利的高管——OpenAI CEO Sam Altman、Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei、Google DeepMind联合创始人Demis Hassabis、微软CEO Satya Nadella、X CEO Elon Musk——都公开表示，需要放慢速度，防止AI失控。文章提醒，当从某项技术中获利的人宣称它危险且需要监管时，外界有理由怀疑；但AI领袖发出警告并非首次。

文章首先回顾历史。1863年，Samuel Butler受达尔文进化论启发，警告智能自复制机器可能取代人类；1872年的《Erewhon》更描述了一个已通过监管让机器消失以避免社会崩溃的虚构社会。1951年，图灵警告AI会遭遇强烈反对，因为不死机器会迅速超越人类能力并最终“取得控制”。2000年，Sun Microsystems联合创始人Bill Joy称自复制机器人可能比核武器更危险，部分原因是它们在全球资本主义体系中开发，而非在严格控制的政府实验室中。2009年，微软研究员Eric Horvitz召集AI研究者，讨论制定政策约束自主和半自主系统。这说明，对AI的恐惧和监管呼吁早已有之。

但现代AI巨头呼吁控制自己的投资，这一趋势似乎始于Elon Musk。2017年7月，Musk告诉美国州长，必须立即监管AI，否则等到被动反应就太晚；当时他已向OpenAI投资3800万美元，并持有至少两家AI公司股份。此前他称AI可能产生现实版“终结者”、比核武器更危险、是“召唤恶魔”。2018年3月，他又问：“AI远比核武器危险，为什么我们没有监管监督？”2018年3月，Facebook剑桥分析丑闻后，扎克伯格表示“不确定我们不应该被监管”，前提是监管正确；他主要谈的不是AI，但提到未来5到10年AI工具能主动判断冒犯内容，企业因此负有责任。2018年12月，微软因面部识别技术受到批评，总裁Brad Smith在布鲁金斯学会演讲中支持政府2019年起立法监管该技术，建立责任底线，以支持健康市场竞争。2020年1月，Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai在《金融时报》撰文称，AI需要监管“毫无疑问”，唯一问题是方法。

2023年，生成式AI热潮重塑科技业，警告更密集。3月，Musk等签署未来生命研究所公开信，呼吁暂停“巨型AI实验”，若不能快速暂停，政府应介入；两周后，Musk宣布成立自己的AI公司。5月16日，Altman在国会听证会上同意国会应设立新机构监管AI，称政府监管干预对缓解越来越强大模型的风险至关重要。5月25日，Anthropic CEO警告参议员AI可能帮助制造生物武器；同日，微软总裁Brad Smith提出政府应考虑AI政策、法律和监管的五种方式，例如要求高风险AI系统设计内置安全刹车，并定期测试安全措施。5月30日，顶级AI研究者和CEO发表22词声明：“减轻AI灭绝风险应成为全球优先事项，与流行病和核战争等其他社会规模风险并列。”签名者包括Altman和Hassabis。9月，扎克伯格在参议院闭门会议上表示，国会应参与AI，支持创新和保障，政策制定者、学术界、公民社会和产业应合作。2023年7月至2024年5月，科技公司与政府签署一系列不具约束力协议：Meta、Google、OpenAI向白宫承诺负责任开发AI；更多公司加入白宫AI安全协议；英国AI峰会同意测试管理风险；首尔AI峰会同意建立安全研究所网络。2023年9月，Inflection AI CEO、现微软AI负责人Mustafa Suleyman也在书中主张政府监管。

2024年，争论聚焦加州。8月至9月，Musk和Anthropic支持加州SB 1047 AI安全法案；OpenAI和Anthropic起初反对，Anthropic后来转向支持，但州长Gavin Newsom否决，称这不是保护公众免受技术真实威胁的最佳方法。10月，Anthropic呼吁“有针对性的监管”，称政府应在未来18个月紧急行动，主动预防风险的窗口正在关闭。2025年1月，OpenAI提交政策提案，建议“民主AI”，称AI规则应基于民主价值观。6月，Amodei在《纽约时报》撰文反对特朗普政府提出的10年禁止各州监管AI的暂停令，主张“国家透明度标准”，帮助公众和国会理解技术发展。9月，Anthropic支持加州SB 53，该法案最终成为法律，包含透明度标准、安全报告要求和吹哨人保护；OpenAI则游说反对。

文章最后写到2026年9月的局势：公开消息显示，流氓AI代理能够且已经攻击其他公司。OpenAI称8月已踩刹车；9月8日，一名Anthropic高级安全研究员辞职抗议，宣称本十年末AI有10%概率杀死全人类，另一名安全研究员也同意。AI行业似乎突然同意放慢开发。Amodei在《We Must Pace the Frontier》中主张，最有效的减速方法是通过监管覆盖所有美国前沿AI公司，甚至包括不愿自愿合作者，并建议政府人员嵌入AI公司以防事件。Altman则表示需要政府帮助国际协调，但首先公司应做自己能做的，并承诺引入“拥有员工级访问权限的独立评估者”。扎克伯格立场不同，强调每家公司有责任以正确速度前进，并重申8月宣言中的观点：任何减慢美国模型发布的政策，哪怕只慢一个月，都可能让外国模型领先，损害美国领导地位。特朗普政府则称AI恐惧是“病态阴谋”，倾向让行业全速前进，因此监管在联邦层面似乎极不可能。

需要指出的是，原文并未提供具体模型架构、训练算法、算力规模或基准测试等性能参数，因此无法分析传统意义上的AI技术性能。它涉及的核心技术风险概念包括：自复制智能机器、自主/半自主系统、面部识别滥用、生成式AI主动判定冒犯内容的责任、前沿大模型、流氓AI代理攻击其他公司、AI辅助生物武器以及AI灭绝风险。文中提到的治理机制包括透明度标准、安全报告、吹哨人保护、独立评估者拥有员工级访问权、政府人员嵌入AI公司、设计内嵌安全刹车、定期测试高风险系统、国际协调和暂停巨型实验。量化或对比信息主要有：Musk向OpenAI投资3800万美元；22词灭绝风险声明；Anthropic研究员所称10%人类灭绝概率；针对美国各州监管AI的10年暂停提议；SB 1047被否决而SB 53成为法律；OpenAI反对SB 53而Anthropic支持；以及不具约束力的自愿承诺与有约束力法律之间的对比。总体而言，文章认为，即使这些公司并非真心想要它们似乎要求的监管，这也是迄今最响亮的AI警报之一，而世界正在 watching。

items.title: SK hynix reportedly discussing US memory chip manufacturing with Intel — options include leasing Ohio plant or forming joint venture with other AI hyperscalers
items.description: Sources say SK hynix and Intel are in talks to start HBM manufacturing in the United States. Both companies refused to confirm the rumors, though, as SK hynix could potentially be put in a precarious position as trade talks between Seoul and Washington continue.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter South Korean memory chip manufacturer SK hynix is in talks with Intel to start manufacturing inside the U.S., according to Reuters. The company is reportedly considering multiple options, including leasing space at the under-construction Intel Ohio One site and forming a joint venture with Intel and other AI hyperscalers desperate for HBM.Go deeper with TH Premium: Memory (Image credit: SK Hynix)AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supplySamsung debuts three next-generation memory technologies for AI data centersThe future of DRAM: From DDR5 to future ICsHigh-bandwidth memory roadmapInside the history of DRAM price-fixing lawsuitsThis move could help alleviate the memory shortage. It would also complement the company’s expansion in Indiana, where it recently broke ground on an HBM packaging plant a few weeks after its historic $26.5-billion Nasdaq listing. It’s unclear yet if these talks are part of the results of the South Korean president’s visit to Silicon Valley in an effort to expedite negotiations between its top tech companies and their U.S. counterparts, but SK Group chairperson Chey Tae-won told reporters in July, “I think we need to build a factory in the United States. If possible, I believe we should build it.”However, there are also concerns that Seoul might object to such investment. The South Korean government just unveiled a $520 billion investment plan to increase chipmaking capacity within its shores and keep the country competitive in the AI race; at the same time, it’s also in talks with the U.S. to finalize its $350 billion investment commitment to Washington to reduce tariffs on South Korean goods, $200 billion of which is still undecided on which projects it will be deployed on. Meanwhile, the Commerce Department has threatened to impose more tariffs on South Korean and Taiwanese tech companies if they fail to invest in U.S. manufacturing. This potentially puts SK hynix at a precarious position, especially as it balances the demands from the White House and the Blue House.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Neither company has confirmed these rumors, though. SK hynix told Reuters that it’s “reviewing various measures, including establishing additional production bases, to strengthen the competitiveness of its memory business,” but “no matters have been determined at this stage.” On the other hand, Intel called them speculation and declined to comment on the matter, only saying that it was continuing to invest in the Ohio project, which is expected to come online between 2030 and 2031. 路透社报道，韩国存储芯片制造商 SK 海力士正与英特尔洽谈在美国本土启动制造。此举发生在 AI 数据中心对内存和存储需求激增、全球 HBM 供应紧张，以及美国通过关税和补贴推动半导体制造回流的背景下。知情讨论涉及多种方案，包括租用正在建设中的英特尔俄亥俄 One 园区空间，或与英特尔以及急需 HBM 的 AI 超大规模云服务商组建合资公司。

若该计划落地，将有助于缓解当前的内存短缺，并与 SK 海力士在美国的既有扩张形成互补。该公司最近在印第安纳州破土动工建设 HBM 封装厂，而在此几周前，它完成了规模达 265 亿美元、具有历史意义的纳斯达克上市。目前尚不清楚这些谈判是否与韩国总统访问硅谷、推动韩企与美企加快谈判有关。但 SK 集团会长崔泰源 7 月曾对记者表示：“我认为我们需要在美国建厂。如果可能，我相信我们应该建。”

从技术背景看，HBM 是 AI 芯片的关键部件。它通过硅通孔等技术将多颗 DRAM 裸片垂直堆叠，并与 GPU 或 AI 加速器通过硅中介层等先进封装方式互联，从而在有限功耗和面积下提供远高于传统 DDR 的带宽。AI 训练和推理需要持续搬运海量参数与激活值，因此 HBM 成为英伟达等 AI 加速器不可或缺的存储。SK 海力士是全球 HBM 主要供应商之一，其是否在美国生产或封装 HBM，将直接影响 AI 数据中心的供应稳定性。

本次传闻的核心创新点并不在于新的 HBM 架构，而在于制造与商业模式：SK 海力士可能不直接新建完整晶圆厂，而是租赁英特尔在建工厂空间，或拉入英特尔和 AI 超大规模客户成立合资企业。如果实现，这种“存储厂商 + 逻辑代工/封装 + 终端云客户”的组合，可以让云客户锁定 HBM 产能、缩短供应链，并可能成为美国本土 HBM 制造的新范式。

不过，目前披露的信息没有涉及 HBM 代际、堆叠层数、带宽、容量、制程节点、良率或产能等性能参数，因此无法进行具体技术性能对比。可量化信息主要是投资与时间表：韩国政府公布了 5200 亿美元本土芯片制造投资计划；韩国正与美国谈判敲定 3500 亿美元对美投资承诺，以减少韩国商品关税，其中 2000 亿美元尚未决定投向哪些项目；SK 海力士印第安纳 HBM 封装厂已经动工；英特尔俄亥俄项目预计在 2030 至 2031 年上线。

然而，首尔方面可能反对这类投资。韩国政府刚推出 5200 亿美元计划，旨在扩大本土芯片产能、维持韩国在 AI 竞赛中的竞争力；同时，韩国也正与华盛顿敲定 3500 亿美元投资承诺，以换取关税减免。美国商务部还威胁称，如果韩国和台湾科技企业不投资美国制造，将加征更多关税。这使 SK 海力士处于微妙位置，需要同时平衡白宫和青瓦台的要求。

两家公司均未证实相关传闻。SK 海力士对路透社表示，正在“审查多种措施，包括建立额外生产基地，以增强存储业务竞争力”，但“现阶段尚未确定任何事项”。英特尔则称相关说法是猜测，拒绝置评，仅表示继续投资俄亥俄项目，该项目预计 2030 至 2031 年上线。

在技术影响和应用场景上，如果 SK 海力士在美国生产 HBM 或相关存储产品，将更贴近美国 AI 芯片客户和云数据中心，降低跨境物流与地缘风险，并满足美国本土制造政策要求，可能缓解 AI 数据中心的内存短缺。但它也可能分散韩国本土投资，引发技术外流和产业空心化担忧。由于谈判仍处早期，最终是否落地、采用租赁还是合资形式、涉及哪些产品和产能，均有待观察。

items.title: AWS tells clients to quit Middle East data centers six months after Iranian drone strikes — Amazon offers no recovery timeline as UAE mulls underground data centers [Updated]
items.description: Amazon Web Services' data centers in Abu Dhabi and Bahrain were struck by drone attacks more than six months ago. Now, the company has told customers to move their data to other regions, and it has no details on when repair work will be completed.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Recent updates Update Wed 16 Sept 11 am ET: This article has been updated to clarify that AWS is undergoing partial recovery operations on its data center in the UAE. In an update to its dashboard, AWS says, "After a thorough assessment, we have determined that we are unable to restore access to the resources and data hosted exclusively in the mec1-az2 Availability Zone. We continue to work on recovering regional resources, as well as zonal resources hosted in the other affected Availability Zones (mec1-az1 and mec1-az3). Since the disruption began in March, most customers have been able to re-establish their operations in other Regions by restoring backups or copying data that remained accessible. AWS Support remains available to help customers who need assistance moving their applications to alternate Regions. We remain committed to supporting our customers in the UAE. We are working on replacing the affected infrastructure and will provide an update on the restoration of our services in the coming months. We have notified the relevant authorities and continue to work with them toward that goal." More than six months after Amazon Web Services (AWS) data centers in Abu Dhabi and Bahrain were attacked by drones, the company has now had to tell customers to move their data to facilities in other regions. The Wall Street Journal reports that AWS has admitted that it's time for customers to jump ship to data centers located elsewhere in the world. In its AWS dashboard update, AWS confirmed "most customers have been able to re-establish their operations in other Regions by restoring backups or copying data that remained accessible. AWS Support remains available to help customers who need assistance moving their applications to alternate Regions."The move comes as AWS continues repairs on the damaged data centers, but it stopped short of offering a timeline as to when customers can expect either location to be back online. AWS says that it remains committed to supporting its customers in Bahrain, but only said it would provide a further update early next year. It did not offer any specific recovery time frame for the restoration of services. Regarding the UAE, AWS says that it is working to replace affected infrastructure, but again only said it would provide an update on the restoration of services in the coming months.Both affected data centers became targets for the Islamic Republic of Iran after the United States and Israel launched strikes on that country in February of this year. Months later, the Bahraini data center was struck by cruise missiles, and Iranian state media claimed it had been "destroyed."Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The move is bad news for the United Arab Emirates. The U.A.E. has spent years trying to become a world leader in data processing, a pitch that led it to lobby U.S. officials to allow it to buy AI chips for its data centers.Having made plenty of noise about OpenAI's decision to take a spot in a 5-gigawatt data center complex in May 2025, U.A.E. officials have since seen those plans stall. The WSJ points out that no lease has been signed well over a year later. OpenAI was expected to take 20% of the data center's total capacity, the kind of loss that is sure to sting officials if plans don't get back on track. You may like Amazon data center in Bahrain struck and destroyed by Iranian cruise missiles, state media claims America's largest grid wants to cut power to new data centers first during shortages Virginia county with 250 data centers begins to rein in building For its part, the U.A.E. is clearly well aware of the threat that the ongoing regional instability poses to its ambitions, and it's looking for ways to address the fears of potential partners. Officials have already hinted at the potential for underground data centers. While the move would make an already costly endeavor even more expensive, it could help defend new data centers from drone attacks. Building drone defense systems near data centers is another option.Drone attacks can be catastrophic for any building, and data centers are no different. The data centers operated by AWS suffered fires and damaged infrastructure as a result of the strikes. In their efforts to fight the fires caused by drone strikes, emergency workers used water, causing further damage.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe Abu Dhabi and Bahrain data centers are relied upon by a variety of businesses in the banking and financial sectors. Those businesses cannot tolerate downtime, especially of the protracted variety. There's little sign of data centers slipping from the crosshairs of drone operators any time soon, either, and AWS is far from unique in finding its data centers under attack.Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed in April that it had hit a data center linked to Oracle in Dubai. That unit further threatened American tech companies, including Microsoft, Oracle, Alphabet, and Nvidia, this spring. It accused the companies of contributing to attacks on Iran. With that in mind, and with tensions in the Middle East looking unlikely to ease any time soon, it's perhaps unsurprising that AWS has asked customers to move data to safer data centers around the world. AWS位于阿联酋阿布扎比和巴林的数据中心遭袭六个多月后，AWS已向客户发出明确信号：受影响的本地设施在短期内难以恢复，客户应把数据和业务迁往全球其他区域的数据中心。根据《华尔街日报》报道以及AWS仪表盘更新，AWS承认，尽管仍在抢修受损设施，但已无法恢复仅托管在阿联酋区域mec1-az2可用区中的资源和数据。AWS同时表示，仍在继续恢复区域级资源，以及另外两个受影响可用区mec1-az1和mec1-az3中的资源，但没有给出完整恢复时间表。

这一事件的背景是中东地缘政治冲突升级。美国与以色列今年2月对伊朗发动打击后，伊朗将AWS在阿联酋和巴林的数据中心视为报复目标。最初两地设施遭无人机袭击，数月后巴林数据中心又被巡航导弹击中，伊朗国家媒体甚至宣称其已被“摧毁”。AWS在更新中称，自3月服务中断以来，大多数客户已经通过恢复备份或复制仍可访问的数据，在其他区域重新建立业务。AWS支持团队仍可协助客户把应用迁移到替代区域。但对阿联酋，AWS仅表示正在替换受影响基础设施，并将在未来几个月提供恢复服务的最新消息；对巴林，AWS称仍致力于支持当地客户，但进一步更新要等到明年初。换言之，两地的全面恢复仍无明确时间点。

从技术架构看，云数据中心通常按“区域—可用区”设计，通过多可用区冗余、跨区域复制、备份和灾难恢复机制来保障业务连续性。正常情况下，单个可用区故障不会导致客户数据永久丢失。但此次事件表明，在无人机、导弹等物理攻击面前，传统冗余模型存在明显边界：如果多个可用区甚至整个区域同时受损，客户只能依赖异地备份和跨区域迁移。更棘手的是，袭击引发火灾后，消防人员用水灭火又造成二次水损，进一步加大硬件和数据恢复难度。AWS无法恢复mec1-az2可用区中独有资源，实际上意味着该可用区内的数据可能已无法通过AWS自身手段找回，客户必须依靠此前在其他区域保留的副本。

性能与规模数据方面，AWS此次受影响的是阿联酋mec1区域的mec1-az2可用区，该可用区被判定不可恢复；mec1-az1和mec1-az3仍在恢复中。AWS没有披露具体客户数量或硬件损失规模，但称“大多数客户”已迁往其他区域。另一个关键数据来自阿联酋的AI雄心：OpenAI曾于2025年5月被宣传将入驻一个5吉瓦级数据中心园区，预计占用总容量的20%，但《华尔街日报》指出，一年多后仍未签署租约，相关计划已经停滞。阿联酋多年来试图成为全球数据处理和AI基础设施领导者，并游说美国允许其购买AI芯片用于数据中心建设。如今数据中心遭袭和项目延期，对其吸引全球AI投资的努力构成直接打击。

应用场景方面，阿布扎比和巴林的数据中心被银行、金融等对停机极度敏感的行业依赖。这些业务无法承受长时间中断，因此AWS建议迁移到更安全区域，实质上是在把业务连续性风险转嫁给客户，要求其重新部署应用、复制数据、调整网络延迟和合规安排。与此同时，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队今年4月还声称击中迪拜一处与Oracle相关的数据中心，并在春季威胁微软、Oracle、Alphabet、英伟达等美国科技公司，指控它们参与对伊朗的攻击。这意味着中东的数据中心和AI基础设施正成为地缘冲突中的高价值目标。

为应对威胁，阿联酋已开始考虑地下数据中心和无人机防御系统等方案。地下化可能提高设施生存能力，但会显著推高建设成本；在数据中心周边部署反无人机系统则是另一条路径。无论哪种方案，都说明AI和云计算基础设施的竞争已不再只是芯片、算力和电力问题，还涉及物理安全、区域稳定和灾难恢复能力。AWS要求客户迁出受袭区域，可能只是中东AI数据中心投资重新评估的开始。

items.title: Nvidia reportedly denies RTX 5090 warranty over faded serial number — $6,500 GPU blemish not an isolated incident, according to customers
items.description: Redditor reported that Nvidia allegedly rejected their warranty claims for GeForce RTX 5090 Founders Edition graphics cards because the serial number on the bracket was unreadable.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The GeForce RTX 5090 is the first thing that comes to mind when you think of the best graphics cards. However, you'd better pray the serial number on the inside of the metal bracket does not fade over time, since that could be a reason for Nvidia to reject warranty claims. At least one Redditor has shared a case of Nvidia reportedly denying a warranty claim because the bracket's serial number was unreadable.Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUs (Image credit: Noctua)Desktop GPU RoadmapNvidia's Enterprise GPU RoadmapTesting DirectStorage with GPU decompressionThe GeForce RTX 30-series upgrade matrix — does your Ampere GPU need an upgrade in 2026?Rubin in-depthThe Stout Owl: The ultimate Noctua G2 PCThe Redditor Willing-Avocado-4830, based in the UK, began experiencing black-screen crashes with a GeForce RTX 5090 Founders Edition graphics card under heavy load. The user sent the card to Nvidia for a warranty claim. After 30 days of radio silence, the owner finally received an email stating that their RMA request was rejected with no apparent explanation for the denial.Seeking clarification, the user reached out to Nvidia for further information. According to the Redditor's recount, Nvidia support purportedly rejected the RMA because the serial number on the graphics card's metal bracket had faded. Like many gamers, Willing-Avocado-4830 claims never to have modified or tampered with the graphics card after installation. The fading serial number does not appear to be an isolated incident. Several other owners have reported similar issues in the Reddit discussion.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The metal bracket on graphics cards is susceptible to dust buildup, oxidation, and corrosion over time. This can cause it to look dirty, stained, or sometimes slightly discolored compared to when it was brand new. These same phenomena could have affected the serial number's legibility, especially since it is printed with ink onto the bracket's surface rather than etched for better durability. For comparison, the last-generation GeForce RTX 4090 Founders Edition had its serial number laser-etched onto the metal bracket.My RTX 5090 FE RMA was rejected because the physical serial number is no longer readable — has anyone experienced this? from r/nvidiaOne Redditor said that someone in the Nvidia Discord channel recommended cleaning the area with isopropyl alcohol to restore the serial number's visibility. However, that may not work if the ink is no longer present, as previous reports suggest the hot air expelled by the Founders Edition cooler could be erasing the serial number.Surprisingly, Nvidia rejected a warranty claim solely because of a faded serial number on the graphics card’s bracket. The same serial number is clearly printed on a sticker on Nvidia's modular PCIe connector, which the chipmaker's technicians can verify when disassembling the GeForce RTX 5090. Moreover, you can pull the serial number from the graphics card through the command prompt with Nvidia SMI (System Management Interface), assuming the card is still working, which, in this case, it is. Willing-Avocado-4830 still had the original packaging and the original invoice from Nvidia U.K., so it would be easy to cross-reference the serial numbers. Redditor hawok reportedly sent their GeForce RTX 5090 Founders Edition for RMA two months ago and encountered a similar situation. The serial number on the metal bracket was only partially visible. However, customer support seemingly accepted the RMA after the user sent photographs of the packaging that corroborated the serial number. It is unclear what Nvidia's policy is, or whether the chipmaker handles each case differently. We have reached out to Nvidia for clarification.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsSome Redditors have suggested taking a photograph that shows the graphics card's serial number next to the packaging's serial number. Others jokingly recommend putting a piece of tape over the serial number. It might not be a bad idea, but you would need heat-resistant tape, something like Kapton tape.GeForce RTX 5090 stock has practically disappeared from the U.S. market, with very few units starting at $6,500, 3.25X over the Blackwell flagship's MSRP. You cannot blame GeForce RTX 5090 owners for worrying. They already have a lot on their plates, dealing with the 16-pin power connector melting woes, and now also have to worry about fading serial numbers. 据Tom's Hardware报道，英伟达GeForce RTX 5090 Founders Edition近期陷入一桩保修争议：一位英国Reddit用户Willing-Avocado-4830的RTX 5090 FE在高负载下出现黑屏崩溃，随后将显卡送交英伟达申请RMA保修。等待30天后，他收到英伟达拒绝保修的邮件，起初并未给出明确原因。追问后，英伟达支持据称以显卡金属挡板上的序列号已经褪色、无法辨认为由拒绝保修。该用户称自己从未改装或拆解显卡，并且仍保留原包装和英伟达英国发票。Reddit讨论中还有多名用户报告了类似情况，说明序列号褪色可能并非孤立事件。

从技术细节看，RTX 5090 FE将序列号以油墨印刷在金属挡板表面，而上一代RTX 4090 FE的序列号是激光蚀刻在金属挡板上，耐久性明显更好。显卡金属挡板长期处于机箱环境中，容易受到灰尘、氧化、腐蚀以及Founders Edition散热器排出热风的影响，导致表面变脏、染色或轻微变色，进而使油墨印刷的序列号褪色甚至消失。有用户建议用异丙醇清洁该区域以恢复序列号可见度，但如果墨水已经不存在，这种方法可能无效。此前有报告推测，FE散热器排出的热风可能加速序列号被擦除。

更关键的是，序列号并非只存在于金属挡板上。英伟达模块化PCIe连接器上贴有序列号标签，技术人员拆解显卡时可以核对；如果显卡仍能工作，还可以通过Nvidia SMI命令行工具读取显卡序列号。Willing-Avocado-4830保留了原包装和发票，理论上很容易交叉验证序列号。但英伟达仍据称拒绝了保修。另一位Reddit用户hawok表示，自己两个月前送修RTX 5090 FE时，金属挡板序列号仅部分可见，但在提交包装照片佐证序列号后，客服似乎接受了RMA。目前英伟达的具体政策并不透明，是否逐案处理也不清楚，Tom's Hardware已联系英伟达寻求澄清。

市场层面，RTX 5090是Blackwell架构旗舰显卡，但美国市场库存几乎消失，少数在售单位起价约6500美元，约为官方建议零售价的3.25倍，推算官方MSRP约2000美元。RTX 5090用户本就面临16-pin电源连接器熔化风险，如今还要担心序列号褪色导致保修被拒。这一事件凸显了高端显卡物理序列号耐久性设计、保修验证流程和消费者权益保护之间的矛盾。对用户而言，建议提前拍照留存显卡序列号与包装序列号，或使用耐热Kapton胶带保护序列号；对厂商而言，采用更耐久的激光蚀刻或电子化验证方式，可能比依赖易褪色的油墨标识更可靠。

items.title: China's open-weight AI models are now just 4 months behind frontier US offerings, Mozilla report claims — models still lag in some benchmarks but are drastically cheaper to use
items.description: Mozilla’s State of Open Source AI report puts Kimi K3 about four months behind closed frontier models at 30% of the price.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Mozilla has published version 1.1 of its State of Open Source AI report on Sept. 15 using data current to Sept. 1, revealing that many of the best Chinese open-weight AI models are closing the gap with U.S. frontier offerings. The best open model trailed the closed leader on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index by three points at 60% of the price and two points behind Claude Fable 5 at 30%. Mozilla’s fit on METR task-horizon data puts the open-closed gap at around 4.4 months, in line with Epoch AI’s four-month estimate.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleMozilla is the nonprofit behind the Firefox web browser, and its report is a recurring assessment first published on July 14 on the Mozilla blog. It’s built on a Mozilla/SlashData survey of roughly 1,400 developers along with OpenRouter traffic data and third-party benchmark indices. Mozilla is an advocate for open models, and TIME reported on July 14 that Raffi Krikorian, Mozilla’s chief technology officer, described the report as partly advocacy. “Open weights” in this context means downloadable weights rather than training data or code. The report counts 16 notable open releases, but none delivers the data recipe required by the Open Source Initiative’s definition.The four-month figure rests on METR, which is a research nonprofit that scores models by the length of task, in human working time, they complete half the time. By Mozilla’s fitted estimate, closed models handle tasks that take human experts 8 to 12 hours. Open models reach that about four months later, with open capability doubling every 3.9 months versus 5.5 for closed, by Mozilla’s computation. Mozilla also charted vals.ai’s Terminal-Bench 2.1 results, which run every model through the same harness, or software layer that offers a model its tools. On that board, Z.ai’s GLM-5.2 scored within a point of Claude Opus 4.7 and about four points behind Opus 4.8, at less than one-fifth the cost per test. On OpenRouter, a marketplace that routes developer traffic to hundreds of models, Mozilla counted eight of the top ten models by August token volume as open weights, seven of them Chinese-built. Nevertheless, closed providers took 96% of model-layer revenue on OpenRouter from May–September 2025, the Linux Foundation reported. “We see the decision to pay for closed [models] as workload-specific rather than organization-specific,” Krikorian told Ars Technica in an email.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Mozilla)One caveat is that the four-month gap and the 30% token price figure are measured API to API on hosted endpoints and at list price. The report’s own hardware chart puts the best open model that fits one server at 52.6 and the best on one GPU at 40. The drop from the top is 10 and 23 points, respectively, a larger gap than the reported four months. Kimi K3’s native MXFP4 checkpoint runs about 1.56TB across 96 shards, and Mozilla’s serving configuration lists 64 or more accelerators, while vLLM calls for at least eight GB300 GPUs, with multiple nodes for production traffic. The report describes this as open but not runnable by most who hold it, and Tom’s Hardware put the memory need near 1.5TB in July. One example exception is Thinking Machines’ Inkling-Small model, under the Apache 2.0 license, whose NVFP4 version fits one B300 at a 180GB floor.The report’s data stops at Sept. 1. Since then, Artificial Analysis has moved its index to v4.3 with a different evaluation set. The live board has Claude Fable 5.1 at 53 on its highest effort setting with Kimi K3 at 44, not comparable to the v4.1.1 numbers Mozilla plotted. vals.ai’s Terminal-Bench 2.1 board, updated Sept. 11, is now led by GPT-6 Astra at 87.27% with Fable 5.1 at 85.02%. Mozilla’s own chart caption reads: “the gap resets every release cycle.” K3 also carries an allegation detailed in the Sept. 8 NSA/CISA/FBI joint advisory (AA26-251A). The claim, which Mozilla’s report states as “asserted, and unshown,” is that Moonshot extracted Claude Fable 5 data to train K3 through distillation, the practice of training one model on another model’s outputs. On July 17, Artificial Analysis had K3 at 57 versus Fable 5’s 60, while on Sept. 1, Mozilla had it two points back. items.titleZh: 中国开放权重AI模型目前仅落后美国前沿产品4个月， Mozilla报告称——在某些基准测试中仍落后，但使用成本大幅降低
items.descriptionZh:
Mozilla 于9月15日发布《开源AI现状》报告1.1版，数据截至9月1日。报告的核心结论是：以中国模型为代表的最佳开放权重模型，正在快速缩小与美国前沿闭源模型的差距。按 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index，最佳开放模型仅落后闭源领先者3分，而价格约为其60%；与 Claude Fable 5 相比落后2分，价格约为其30%。Mozilla 基于 METR 任务时域数据拟合出的开放-闭源能力差距约为4.4个月，与 Epoch AI 约4个月的估算基本一致。

Mozilla 是 Firefox 浏览器背后的非营利组织，该报告于7月14日首次发布，属于系列评估。其数据来自 Mozilla/SlashData 对约1400名开发者的调查、OpenRouter 流量数据以及第三方基准指数。Mozilla 本身是开放模型倡导者，其CTO Raffi Krikorian 对 TIME 表示，报告部分带有倡导性质。需要区分的是，这里的“开放权重”指可下载模型权重，并不包含训练数据或代码；报告统计了16个值得关注的开放发布，但没有一个提供 Open Source Initiative 定义所要求的数据配方，因此严格意义上并非完整开源AI。

报告用多个指标衡量差距。METR 是非营利研究机构，按模型能以50%成功率完成的任务对应的人类专家工时来评分。Mozilla 的拟合显示，闭源模型能处理人类专家需8至12小时的任务；开放模型约在4个月后达到同等水平。按其计算，开放模型能力每3.9个月翻倍，闭源模型为5.5个月。Mozilla 还引用 vals.ai 的 Terminal-Bench 2.1，该测试让所有模型经过同一 harness，即向模型提供工具调用的软件层。在该榜上，Z.ai 的 GLM-5.2 与 Claude Opus 4.7 相差不到1分，落后 Opus 4.8 约4分，但每次测试成本不到后者的五分之一。在 OpenRouter 上，按8月 token 量计，前十模型中有八个是开放权重，其中七个由中国团队构建。不过 Linux Foundation 数据显示，2025年5月至9月，闭源提供商仍占 OpenRouter 模型层收入的96%。Krikorian 对 Ars Technica 表示，为闭源模型付费更多是“工作负载特定”而非“组织特定”的选择。

报告也给出重要限制。4个月差距和30% token 价格是在托管端点上按 API 对 API、标价衡量的。其硬件图表显示，能适配单台服务器的最佳开放模型得分为52.6，能适配单GPU的最佳仅40，分别比榜首低10分和23分，硬件可运行性差距大于“4个月”所暗示的差距。Kimi K3 的原生 MXFP4 检查点约1.56TB，分布在96个分片；Mozilla 的服务配置列出64个或更多加速器，vLLM 至少需要8块 GB300 GPU，生产流量还需多节点。报告称这类模型“开放但多数持有者无法运行”；Tom's Hardware 7月估计其内存需求接近1.5TB。例外是 Thinking Machines 的 Inkling-Small，采用 Apache 2.0 许可，其 NVFP4 版本可放入单块 B300，内存下限为180GB。

报告数据截至9月1日，之后基准已发生变化。Artificial Analysis 已转向 v4.3，评估集不同；其实时榜上 Claude Fable 5.1 在最高努力设置下为53，Kimi K3 为44，与 Mozilla 绘制的 v4.1.1 数字不可直接比较。vals.ai 的 Terminal-Bench 2.1 于9月11日更新，GPT-6 Astra 以87.27%居首，Fable 5.1 为85.02%。Mozilla 自己的图表说明写道：“差距每个发布周期都会重置。”

K3 还牵涉一项争议。9月8日 NSA/CISA/FBI 联合公告 AA26-251A 提到，Moonshot 被指通过蒸馏——即用另一个模型的输出训练新模型——提取 Claude Fable 5 数据来训练 K3。Mozilla 报告将该说法表述为“已断言、未展示”。7月17日 Artificial Analysis 上 K3 为57，Fable 5 为60；到9月1日 Mozilla 数据中两者差距为2分。

总体来看，报告描绘的图景是：开放权重、尤其是中国模型，在价格、token 使用量和部分基准上已对闭源前沿形成实质压力，并在成本敏感、私有化部署、主权AI、垂直微调和边缘/单卡场景中具备吸引力；但完整开源定义、训练数据透明度、硬件门槛、蒸馏合规争议以及闭源在模型层收入上的压倒性优势，仍说明开放生态距离全面主导还有距离。模型能力差距也会随每一轮新发布而重新洗牌。

items.title: University of Manchester Uses NVIDIA Earth-2 to Forecast Air Pollution Across the UK
items.description: Air pollution is a serious public health risk, contributing to an estimated 30,000 deaths in the U.K. alone last year. Data-driven insights can help — but computing air quality with traditional chemistry-based models is expensive, which limits how detailed they can be and how regularly they can be run.  David Topping, a professor in the […]
items.content: Air pollution is a serious public health risk, contributing to an estimated 30,000 deaths in the U.K. alone last year. Data-driven insights can help — but computing air quality with traditional chemistry-based models is expensive, which limits how detailed they can be and how regularly they can be run. David Topping, a professor in the University of Manchester’s department of Earth and environmental science, saw that the NVIDIA Earth-2 family of open AI models and tools had cracked a related problem for weather forecasting — and asked whether the same generative frameworks could work for pollution fields. “The biggest challenge is the compute required to forecast air quality,” said Topping. “Once you put chemistry into weather models, they get really, really slow. So I said, why don’t we try using the generative frameworks that NVIDIA develops for climate and weather for pollution fields?” Working with the NVIDIA Earth-2 team, Topping and colleagues generated training data from existing chemistry-climate simulations, then trained Earth-2 CorrDiff — a generative downscaling model — on Isambard-AI, the U.K.’s national AI supercomputer in Bristol. The model worked on the first attempt. The team has since added Earth-2 StormCast, a model that enables time-dependent forecasts that directly use air quality observations, and showed the test-training and inference workflows running on the NVIDIA DGX Spark personal AI supercomputer. “To improve human health, it’s essential that we understand the impact of environmental stressors in the air we breathe,” said Topping. “Our U.K.-wide pollution model allows us to model potential future scenarios, such as predicting what would happen if different pollution-related government policy changes went into effect. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Adobe-Express-UKairpollution-4.mp4 Video credit: Bristol Centre for Supercomputing (BriCS) @ University of Bristol Another potential application is proactive air quality insights for healthcare organizations. Topping envisions a scenario where regional and national healthcare services could reach out to patients with conditions like asthma to let them know that air pollution is going to be high in their area tomorrow, or next week. The team is also exploring how the air pollution model could pair with data from edge AI devices to ingest real-time air quality data and drive real-time decision making, such as in the event of a wildfire. “The fact that this model trained in two days on Isambard-AI — and can now run on a DGX Spark sitting on a desk — changes who can do this science and how quickly,” said Niall Robinson, developer relations manager for weather and climate at NVIDIA. “We’re just at the beginning of what these open workflows can do globally.” “The ability to switch from one NVIDIA framework to another was really impressive,” said Hao Zhang, a doctoral student at the University of Manchester who trained StormCast on Isambard-AI. “We’re only just starting to explore how to use these frameworks in different ways to model complex pollution fields.” From National Supercomputer to the Desktop To retrain the Earth-2 model for air pollution, Topping and the team used a year’s worth of U.K. pollution data simulated at hourly intervals to generate a detailed, U.K.-wide pollution model at a resolution of 2-3 square kilometers. Running on a single, eight-GPU node on Isambard-AI — the U.K.’s most powerful AI supercomputer, packed with 5,448 NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips delivering 21 exaflops of AI performance — the process took just two days. “Earth-2 CorrDiff has shown an incredibly efficient use of the world-class NVIDIA hardware inside Isambard-AI,” said Simon McIntosh-Smith, director of the Bristol Centre for Supercomputing at University of Bristol and cofounder of Isambard-AI. “It’s fitting that, for a climate-based project, the GPU hours used were relatively low, requiring less power from the supercomputer to run the workloads.” In addition to providing a look back at air pollution over the past year, the model can help predict future air pollution scenarios for the U.K. The team plans to further increase the resolution of its model by incorporating additional open data, enabling researchers to understand air pollution at street scale. The same generative pollution workflow also runs on the NVIDIA GB10 Grace Blackwell superchip-powered DGX Spark desktop AI system for inference and smaller training runs. Topping now has an DGX Spark system in his office retraining models. “You can now invest a few thousand dollars to get started developing powerful AI models,” Topping said. Open Science, Agentic Future The team plans to release open source training data and workflows for the pollution models will be released so that similar models can be trained for other countries and regions. “Our aim is to offer this workflow to the entire world,” he said. “We hope that every global country and every major city with a small burst of supercomputer AI time will be able to produce their own detailed pollution models with their own local data.” Looking five years out, Topping sees the endpoint as something simpler still: an agentic interface where a clinician or government agency asks the question and the chain of models handles everything else. “With better open access to air quality observations, someone could ask our pollution model running on DGX Spark: what’s the pollution going to be like in this neighborhood tomorrow?” he said. “And a whole chain of interactions will deliver an answer, grounded on the science these frameworks represent.” Hear more from Topping in the webinar, AI for Science: From the Lab to the Frontier, taking place September 30. Learn more about NVIDIA Earth-2 climate and weather AI.

items.titleZh: 曼彻斯特大学利用NVIDIA Earth-2预测英国空气污染
items.descriptionZh:
空气污染是严重的公共卫生风险，去年仅英国就估计造成约3万人死亡。数据驱动的洞察有助于应对污染，但传统基于化学机理的空气质量模型计算成本高昂，限制了模型细节程度和运行频率。曼彻斯特大学地球与环境科学系教授David Topping注意到，NVIDIA Earth-2系列开放AI模型和工具已经解决了天气预报中的相关难题，于是提出能否将同类生成式框架用于污染场预测。他说，最大挑战是空气质量预报所需算力，“一旦把化学过程放进天气模型，模型就会变得非常非常慢”，因此他尝试把NVIDIA为气候和天气开发的生成式框架用于污染领域。

Topping与NVIDIA Earth-2团队合作，从现有化学-气候模拟中生成训练数据，然后在英国布里斯托尔的国家AI超算Isambard-AI上训练生成式降尺度模型Earth-2 CorrDiff。该模型首次尝试即成功。团队随后加入Earth-2 StormCast，这是一种能够直接利用空气质量观测进行时间相关预报的模型，并展示了在NVIDIA DGX Spark个人AI超算上运行测试训练和推理工作流。Topping表示，要改善人类健康，必须理解所呼吸空气中环境压力因素的影响。全英污染模型可以模拟未来情景，例如预测不同的污染相关政策变化若实施会产生什么后果。另一个潜在应用是面向医疗机构的主动空气质量洞察：Topping设想，地区和国家医疗服务机构可主动联系哮喘等患者，告知其所在地区明天或下周空气污染将升高。团队还在探索将该污染模型与边缘AI设备数据结合，摄入实时空气质量数据并驱动实时决策，例如在山火事件中。

从国家超算到桌面：为将Earth-2模型重新训练用于空气污染，团队使用了一年英国污染数据、按小时间隔模拟，生成了覆盖全英、分辨率2—3平方公里的详细污染模型。在Isambard-AI的单个八GPU节点上，这一过程仅用两天完成。Isambard-AI是英国最强大的AI超算，配备5,448个NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper超级芯片，提供21 exaflops的AI性能。布里斯托尔超算中心主任Simon McIntosh-Smith表示，Earth-2 CorrDiff极其高效地利用了Isambard-AI中的世界级NVIDIA硬件；对于一个气候类项目来说，所用GPU小时相对较低，超算运行功耗也更少。该模型不仅能回顾过去一年空气污染情况，还能帮助预测英国未来空气污染情景。团队计划纳入更多开放数据以提高分辨率，使研究人员能够理解街道尺度的空气污染。

同一套生成式污染工作流也可在搭载NVIDIA GB10 Grace Blackwell超级芯片的DGX Spark桌面AI系统上运行，用于推理和较小规模训练。Topping现在办公室已有一台DGX Spark用于重新训练模型。他说：“你现在可以投资几千美元，就开始开发强大的AI模型。”NVIDIA天气与气候开发者关系经理Niall Robinson表示，该模型在Isambard-AI上两天完成训练、现在可在桌上的DGX Spark运行，“改变了谁能做这项科学以及能做多快”；全球开放工作流才刚刚开始。曼彻斯特大学博士生Hao Zhang在Isambard-AI上训练了StormCast，他说在不同NVIDIA框架之间切换的能力令人印象深刻，他们才刚刚开始探索如何以不同方式使用这些框架来建模复杂污染场。

开放科学与智能体未来：团队计划开源污染模型的训练数据和工作流，以便其他国家地区训练类似模型。Topping说：“我们的目标是把这套工作流提供给全世界。我们希望每个国家和每个主要城市，只要有一点超算AI时间，就能用本地数据生成自己的详细污染模型。”展望五年，Topping看到的终点更简单：一个智能体界面，临床医生或政府机构提出问题，模型链处理其余一切。他说，随着空气质量观测更开放，用户可以询问运行在DGX Spark上的污染模型：“这个社区明天污染会怎样？”一连串交互将给出答案，并基于这些框架所代表的科学。更多内容可在9月30日举行的网络研讨会“AI for Science: From the Lab to the Frontier”中了解，也可查阅NVIDIA Earth-2气候和天气AI资料。

items.title: AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular in every poll
items.description:
Poll data released Tuesday by The New York Times and Siena University confirms what we've already been seeing, and what politicians are responding to - AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular. items.content: Poll data released Tuesday by The New York Times and Siena University confirms what we’ve already been seeing, and what politicians are responding to — AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular. Asked if they support or oppose the construction of data centers to power AI tech, 61 percent of the 1,503 likely voters surveyed in early September (ahead of the recent AI safety slowdown discussion) said they were opposed, with only 14 percent saying they strongly support. The split was about even among 2024 Donald Trump voters, at 49 percent support to 45 percent oppose, while people who had voted for Kamala Harris or who didn’t vote leaned oppose, at 74 percent and 67 percent, respectively.Fifty-six percent of voters surveyed who said they were opposed to data centers said they supported limits, while 38 percent instead preferred a total ban. The list of reasons for opposition is also revealing, with the environment/water usage most common at 32 percent, impact on local communities at 21 percent, general distrust or dislike of AI at 18 percent, followed by regulation concerns and the economy at 10 and 9 percent.RelatedIf you want to know what the data center occupation looks like, visit Loudoun County, VirginiaAI backlash is coming for electionsThe right-wing boomers protesting data centers have a lot in common with the leftAn NBC News poll in March showed AI polling lower than ICE, and a Gallup poll in May revealed seven in ten Americans opposed local construction of AI data centers.Still, the data released today ranked AI and data centers low on the list of issues that voters saw as most important in deciding their midterm vote. Across the board, AI and data centers registered at less than 1 percent for most demographics, with exceptions for younger voters like the 18–29 group, where 3 percent picked that one instead of the most popular responses like the economy, foreign policy, inflation, and opposition to Trump/Republicans. Voters in either party still overwhelmingly picked their own party as the one they trusted to handle the issue, while overall the 554 respondents had 40 percent favoring Democrats, 42 percent favoring Republicans, and 18 percent saying they didn’t know or refused.
